habitat: Any woodland, including mopane, mixed bushveld and riverine forest. It is often seen by day and is frequently mobbed by small birds.
summary: A common resident. A very small earless owl. The upperparts are brown with small white spots, and the underparts are white, streaked brown, with pearl-like spots. Two black marks on the nape look like eyes. The call is a long ascending series of tee notes, then a descending series. The Kemp name Pearlspotted Owl and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: African Barred Owlet is larger and dumpier, with fine barring above and a row of bold white wing spots.

head.pattern: Earless. Two black marks on the nape look like eyes.

upperparts.pattern: Dark brown-grey above, well spotted white. The description says brown with small white spots.

underparts.pattern: White below, streaked brown, with pearl-like spots.

viewNotes.note: White underparts streaked brown, with pearl-like spots.
Two black marks on the nape, and white spots on the brown upperparts.
Very small and earless, spotted white above.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: A long ascending 'tee-tee-tee…', then, after a pause, a descending 'teeew, teeew, tew, tew…'. It is often heard by day. The grade A call is from Thabazimbi. The filename is XC194518-2014-09-06 10_23 ps owlet x 2.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Dark brown-grey is not stored as one back colour. The grade A call is from Limpopo, not from inside Kruger. The Kemp name Pearlspotted Owl and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^14=16384 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 8192–32768.
